fieldData.short-description: Smooth, sweet, and balanced. This vanilla salted matcha latte blends creamy vanilla with a subtle touch of sea salt to enhance the natural umami of matcha.
fieldData.ingredients:
‍

Salted Vanilla Matcha Latte

‍

Smooth, sweet, and balanced. This vanilla salted matcha latte blends creamy vanilla with a subtle touch of sea salt to enhance the natural umami of matcha. Comforting yet refreshing, it’s a favourite all year round.

‍

What you’ll need:

‍
- 3g ceremonial matcha powder (we used our East China Ceremonial)
- 40ml warm water (max 80°C)
- 150ml milk of choice
- ½ tsp vanilla extract or vanilla syrup
- Sweetener to taste (optional)
- A small pinch of sea salt
- Ice (for iced version)

‍

How to make it:

‍

Whisk the matcha
Sift 3g of matcha powder into a bowl. Add the warm water and whisk until smooth and lightly frothy with no clumps.

‍

Prepare the vanilla base
Add your milk to a glass (with ice if making iced). Stir in the vanilla and sweetener if using. Add a very small pinch of sea salt and mix well to combine.

‍

Bring it together
Gently pour the whisked matcha over the milk. For a layered effect, pour slowly over the ice or the back of a spoon.

‍

Sip and savour
Enjoy the creamy sweetness of vanilla balanced with a delicate salty finish that enhances the depth of the matcha. Smooth, comforting, and perfectly rounded.
fieldData.name: Salted Vanilla Matcha Latte

  • 40ml warm water (max 80°C)

Whisk the matcha
Sift 3g of matcha powder into a bowl. Add warm water and whisk until smooth and lightly frothy.

fieldData.short-description: A lavender matcha latte that delivers smooth, sustained energy with a gentle floral touch.
fieldData.ingredients:
‍

A lavender matcha latte that delivers smooth, sustained energy with a gentle floral touch.

‍

What you’ll need:

‍

For the Lavender Matcha Latte:

  • 3g matcha (for this recipe we used our Shizuoka Ceremonial)
  • 40ml warm water (max 75°C)
  • 200ml milk of choice (oat or almond work beautifully)
  • 15ml lavender syrup* (adjust to taste)

*Lavender syrup can be homemade by gently heating sugar, water, and culinary lavender, then straining.

‍

Decoration (optional):

  • Dried (culinary) lavender buds
  • Fresh lavender sprig
  • Light milk foam or matcha dusting

‍

How to make it:

‍

Whisk the matcha
Sift 3g of matcha into a matcha bowl (we used our Shizuoka Ceremonial). Add warm water and whisk with a chasen until smooth and lightly frothy.

‍

Flavour the milk
Add your preferred milk with ice in the glass and stir in the lavender syrup until delicately floral.

‍

Bring it together
Gently add the whisked matcha on top of the ice* for a beautiful green contrast.

*Tip: If you pour slowly on top of the ice, you will create those beautiful layers of milk and matcha on top.

‍

Garnish
Finish with a sprinkle of dried lavender, a little foam, or a dusting of matcha.

‍

Sip and unwind
Take a moment, breathe in that floral aroma, and enjoy your calm and creamy lavender matcha latte.

‍

A little tip:
Lavender is powerful, so start light and add more only if needed. This latte is not meant to taste like lavender soap.
fieldData.name: Lavender Matcha Latte

fieldData.short-description: Soothing, smokey and spiced. This hojicha chai (aka hojichai) latte is the perfect drink to wind down with.
fieldData.ingredients:
‍

Soothing, smokey and spiced. This hojicha chai (aka hojichai) latte is the perfect drink to wind down with.

‍

What you’ll need:

‍

For the Hojicha Chai Latte:

  • 3g hojicha powder (we used our Organic Kyoto Hojicha)
  • 40ml warm water (max 80°C)
  • 200ml milk of choice (oat milk pairs beautifully)
  • 15–20ml chai syrup (adjust to taste)

‍

Optional topping:

  • Star anise
  • Cinnamon

‍

How to make it:

‍

Whisk the hojicha
Sift 3g of hojicha powder into a bowl. Add warm water and whisk until smooth and lightly frothy.

‍

Spice up the milk
Add your milk and ice to the glass and gently pour in your chai syrup*.

‍

*No chai syrup? Make your own:
Simmer 250ml water with:

  • 1 cinnamon stick
  • 3-4 cardamom pods (lightly crushed)
  • 3 cloves
  • ½ tsp ground ginger or a few slices of fresh ginger
  • 1 star anise
  • Black peppercorns (optional)

‍

Let it simmer for 10–15 minutes, then strain. Add sugar to taste while warm and stir until dissolved. Store in the fridge and use as needed.

‍

Bring it together
Gently add the whisked hojicha to your chai milk, make sure to pour slowly on the ice to get distinguished layers.

‍

Finish
Float a star anise on top for a decorative touch.

‍

Sip and savour
Enjoy the mellow roasted notes of hojicha wrapped in warming chai spices, this combination is grounding, smooth, and deeply comforting.
fieldData.name: Hojicha Chai Latte

fieldData.short-description: The combination of the roasted notes of hojicha, nuttiness of hazelnut and mellow sweetness of maple syrup blend perfectly together for a comforting and cozy drink.
fieldData.ingredients:
- 2.5 grams of hojicha 
- 1 tbsp maple syrup 
- 150ml hazelnut milk 
- 50ml hot water (around 75°C / 175°F)
- Ice (optional, if you prefer it iced)
- Hazelnuts (optional)
fieldData.directions:
How To Make It:
‍Whisk the Hojicha in a matcha bowl, sift your hojicha powder.
Add hot water and whisk with a chasen until smooth and slightly frothy.

The roasted notes should start to bloom, creating a nutty aroma that pairs perfectly with the maple syrup and hazelnut milk.

‍(Optional) Add a hazelnut rim
Adding a rim of chopped hazelnuts can elevate your drink and is more effortless than it looks. By dipping the rim in maple syrup, it creates a ‘glue’ that will enable the chopped hazelnuts to stick. 

‍Pour and Enjoy
Pour your whisked hojicha into a prepared glass of hazelnut milk with ice. By pouring slowly on top of the ice, you will get beautiful layers that float on top of one another.

To drink, gently stir to blend the hazelnut milk with the rich, toasted flavors of the hojicha, or let the layers swirl naturally for a beautiful presentation.
fieldData.name: Hazelnut Maple Hojicha Latte

fieldData.short-description: The smooth sweetness of white chocolate and the earthy notes of matcha come together in these easy Christmas tree chocolates for a festive bite.
fieldData.ingredients:
Easy and quick matcha Christmas tree chocolates

‍

‍

You’ll need:

- 2 white chocolate bars

- Matcha powder (to taste), we used about 3 grams of our Organic Culinary Japan

- Optional: pretzels + any toppings you like (sprinkles, crushed candy canes, nuts, etc.)
fieldData.directions:
How to make:

1. Break one white chocolate bar into its little squares.

2. Chop each square into triangle shapes to look like Christmas trees and et aside.

3. Take all the chopped-off bits plus the second white chocolate bar and melt them gently (microwave in short bursts or au bain marie).

4. Stir in matcha powder until you get a nice green colour and smooth texture.

5. Dip the chocolate triangles into the matcha chocolate and place on baking paper to cool.I also dipped some pretzels at this stage

6. Once everything has set, melt the leftover matcha chocolate again and pour it into a small bag (a freezer bag works!), cut off a tiny corner, and drizzle over the chocolates.

7. Add toppings if you want, let them cool completely, and voila! you’re done
fieldData.name: Easy Matcha Christmas Chocolates

fieldData.short-description: The vibrant umami of matcha, bright citrus notes, and a touch of gentle sweetness come together for a refreshing yet festive martini.
fieldData.ingredients:
‍

What you’ll need:

‍

For the Matchini:

  • 3g of matcha
  • 40ml of water
  • 10ml vodka
  • 20ml white rum
  • 15ml simple syrup (can be homemade using a 1:1 sugar and water mixture heated until the sugar is dissolved)
  • A squeeze of lemon juice

Mocktail version: for an alcohol free version, you can replace the alcohol for 20ml of pear juice.

Decoration (optional):

  • White sugar rim
  • Rosemary stalk (your mini Christmas tree!)
  • Cranberries
fieldData.directions:
How to make it:

‍

Whisk the matcha

‍
In a matcha bowl, sift your 3 grams of ceremonial matcha powder (we used our Shizuoka Ceremonial). Add warm water (not more than 75°C) and whisk with a chasen until smooth and frothy.

‍

Optional: Add a ‘snowy’ white sugar rim:

‍Dip the rim of your glass in water to create a ‘glue’, then coat with white sugar.

‍

Let your inner mixologist come out
Pour in the vodka, rum, simple syrup, a splash of lemon juice, the frothy matcha and ice into your cocktail shaker and jingle it all the way for about 10-15 seconds.

‍

Garnish
Add a sprig of rosemary and a few cranberries to add a little christmas spirit to your matchini.

‍

Pour and enjoy
Raise your glass and toast to a wonderful “matcha-mas”.

‍

A little tip: Sip slowly because this Merry Matchini is smooth enough to sleigh you right into holiday spirit!
fieldData.name: Merry Matchini
